source.title: Hard Sample Aware Noise Robust Learning for Histopathology Image Classification
source.authors: Chuang Zhu; Wenkai Chen; T. Peng; Ying Wang; M. Jin

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures learning and forgetting events for hard and noisy samples over training, bearing on whether they are learned differently over time (V6), using a different measure from the original studies.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work on memorization, but those cited results are not this study's results. Its own training-event analysis in Section G bears on V6; its noisy-label classification results do not measure the other claim versions.
record.test_reason: Section IV.G measures changes in learning and forgetting events during training for hard clean versus noisy samples. These results bear on V6 through a different measure of learning dynamics. The noise-robust classification accuracies do not establish V1–V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but narrow. The authors conclude that prediction histories distinguish hard clean from noisy samples, enabling their correction scheme to retain more hard clean samples; their subsequent training scheme further suppresses noise and improves classification performance.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes hard-sample-aware noisy-label correction and training for histopathology classification; it does not reproduce the original random-label experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Hard samples have higher learning and forgetting event frequencies over the whole training period.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hard clean samples undergo more prediction-threshold transitions than noisy samples.

record.problems: The event-frequency results are presented in a figure without numeric values or reported uncertainty. The paper does not state the dataset condition for this event analysis in the relevant passage.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows were omitted; the paper's other noisy-label accuracy and ablation results do not measure any of the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Complete random labeling, near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training-time comparisons between true and random labels and convergence slowdown across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit throughout a corruption sweep and test error rising toward chance. Reported test accuracies alone do not establish this joint claim.
Whether explicit regularization prevents random-label fitting or is necessary for generalization on true labels.
Direct measurement of shared-pattern acquisition, a completely random-label comparison, and eventual memorization of all noisy labels. Threshold-crossing events do not establish sustained fitting.

missing.what: Selected noisy samples located centrally within the opposite class remain difficult to predict late in training, with histories compared against hard clean samples. This supplies additional evidence about differing training dynamics, but does not establish eventual noise memorization. The comparison is selective and has no numerical summary in the supplied text.
missing.locator: Section IV.G, Figs. 19–20; Camelyon16 with 20% label noise

record.verdict_notes: Learning and forgetting are defined by upward and downward crossings of 0.5 probability for the assigned label. Hard clean samples are selected through low mean assigned-label probability, so this is a selected subgroup comparison. No numerical event frequencies or uncertainty are recoverable from the supplied text. ImageNet pretraining is stated for Fig. 19 feature extraction and should not be assumed for Fig. 17.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test fitting completely random labels, training error on them, test error at chance, or whether the architecture and training hyperparameters remain unchanged.
No comparison of training time for true versus random labels, or convergence speed across corruption levels.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
The paper reports test accuracy under label noise but does not establish perfect training fit or steadily rising test error toward chance while retaining signal.
No test of weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation as barriers to fitting random labels or as necessary conditions for generalization.
The analysis concerns hard and noisy samples in a noisy-label histopathology setting; it does not compare clean real labels against completely random labels or directly measure when each is fitted.

rows.subject: Resnet-34
rows.operation_detail: Counted learning and forgetting events for hard and noisy samples during training.
rows.measure: Relative frequency of learning and forgetting events for hard versus noisy samples
rows.value: In the early stage, hard samples tend to have more learning events, while noisy samples tend to have more forgetting events.
rows.note: The paper describes the direction of the result in text; the plotted frequency values are not given numerically.
rows.check: The qualitative early-training comparison is accurately reported in the text, so evidence_form should include textual evidence. The passage does not explicitly identify the model, dataset, noise ratio, or training procedure for Fig. 17; ResNet-34 is inferred from the broader medical experiments.

rows.subject: Resnet-34
rows.operation_detail: Counted learning and forgetting events for hard and noisy samples during training.
rows.measure: Relative frequency of learning and forgetting events for hard versus noisy samples
rows.value: In the late stage, hard samples tend to have more forgetting events, while noisy samples tend to have more learning events.
rows.note: The paper describes the direction of the result in text; the plotted frequency values are not given numerically.
rows.check: The qualitative late-training comparison is accurately reported in the text, so evidence_form should include textual evidence. The specific experimental condition and model for Fig. 17 are not explicitly identified.

rows.subject: Resnet-34
rows.operation_detail: Compared learning and forgetting event frequencies across the full training period.
rows.measure: Learning and forgetting event frequency for hard versus noisy samples
rows.value: The frequency of learning and forgetting events of hard samples is higher than that of noisy samples during the whole training epochs.
rows.note: The paper states this comparison in text; numerical frequencies are not reported.
rows.check: The pooled event-frequency comparison is accurately paraphrased, but it does not establish temporal learning order or differences across training stages. Higher total transition frequency alone cannot show V6.

relationships.condition: Hard clean versus noisy samples in the Fig. 17 training analysis; exact dataset and noise condition unspecified
relationships.reason: R1 reports more early learning events for hard clean samples, while R2 reports more late learning events for noisy samples, supporting different temporal learning dynamics.
relationships.display_finding: Hard clean samples had more early learning events, whereas noisy samples had more late learning events.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Hard and noisy samples during training in the analyzed histopathology setting
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports different event patterns by sample type, with hard samples learning more in the early stage and noisy samples learning more in the late stage (R1–R3). This is evidence of different training behavior, not a direct measurement of label-fitting order.
